column1: # Curated dish catalogue for the day planner.
# What this is for: the fortnight before a profile has any saved recipes of its own. The planner
# always prefers the user's meals over these, and should — a recipe somebody wrote down is in
# their words, made of food they buy. These exist so that day one is not a list of ingredients.
# Capped at sixty. Reshuffling has to stay interesting only until the recipe book fills up, and
# every dish here costs eleven translations of its name.
# `id` is permanent the way a food id is. `slots` are lowercased names from `_splits` in
# A part is `fid:role:grams` with an optional fourth field, the step a `unit` moves in:
#   fixed   the cup of coffee, the splash of milk in it. Never resized.
#   unit    slices, eggs, tortillas. Whole multiples of the step — two or three, never 2.4.
#   flex    the anchor, and where protein is bought.
#   accent  the cheese, the olives. Something you have a piece of, capped at twice the recipe.
#   side    the salad, the vegetables. Where spare calories go.
#   trace   the oil it was cooked in.
# The bands each role implies live in lib/domain/day_plan_source.dart, not here: one place to
# change them, and no regeneration needed to do it. Grams are one honest serving of the dish as
# written — the planner scales from there.
# Whole ingredients only. There is no stock, no spice and no vinegar in the food catalogue, and
# a dish that leans on one would price out wrong. Seasoning is assumed, not listed.
